To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the MAOA gene was linked to brain activity in the frontoparietal attention network, that this brain activity was correlated to visuospatial working memory capacity, and that visuospatial working capacity in turn predicted externalization symptoms.
a polymorphism (rs6609256) in the MAOA gene was associated with visuospatial working memory brain activity, which in turn was correlated to visuospatial working capacity and externalizing symptoms.

a single-nucleotide variant in a gene located ∼6 kb downstream from the monoamine oxidace A (MAOA) gene is associated with brain activity in a large network of regions, including frontal, parietial and occipital cortices; this variant is also correlated with visuospatial working memory capacity, which is, in turn, correlated with externalizing symptoms, with higher working memory capacity associated with fewer symptoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of brain activity and capacity during childhood and adolescence, with the aim to identify the neurobiological mechanisms linking genes to aggressive behavior.
understanding the neurobiological mechanisms that underlie cognitive development and how these mechanisms are linked to genetic and environmental factors.
the role of working memory (WM)-related brain activity in gene–brain–development–behavior relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MAOA gene, via the brain activity of a WM network and VSWM capacity, influences the development of aggressive behavior in typically developing children and adolescent.
the rs6609257 polymorphism in the MAOA gene affects the brain activity in a fronto-parieto-occipital network during VSWM.
the rs6609257 variant in MAOA is related to brain activity in a fronto-parietal network, which in turn is associated with VSWM capacity and externalizing behavioral problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MAOA gene is related to brain activity and capacity for visuospatial working memory, which is related to externalizing symptoms, but that the MAOA polymorphism is not related to externalizing behaviors directly.
the MAOA gene is related to aggressive behavior in a developmental context by affecting WM brain activity and VSWM capacity.
a developmental increase in WM brain activity is an important part in cognitive development, and that low WM brain activity is a risk factor to develop psychopathology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MAOA gene is linked to aggressive behavior during adolescence, and that the mechanism of this effect may be via working memory brain activity and working memory capacity.
we have identified a gene that is associated with brain activity during working memory, which in turn predicts externalizing behaviors, which in turn are associated with aggressive behavior.
brain activity in a large network of regions is more important for predicting behavior than activity in specific regions.
